subject.title: fix(infra): cap process-lifetime env-log dedupe cache with bounded DedupeCache

question: Should environment-option logging remain exactly once per key for the process lifetime, or intentionally become a 1,024-key best-effort window?
rationale: Bounding memory and preserving exact lifetime deduplication cannot both be achieved with this evicting cache, while the current evidence does not show a production path that needs the tradeoff.

options.title: Preserve Once-Only Semantics
options.body: Keep the lifetime Set or move any necessary bound to a demonstrated dynamic-key caller so existing logging behavior remains exact.

options.title: Accept Bounded Best-Effort Logging
options.body: Document the eviction behavior and add reviewable real-Gateway evidence showing that dynamic-key growth is reachable and materially affects memory.

recommendation.title: Preserve Once-Only Semantics
recommendation.body: Keep the lifetime Set or move any necessary bound to a demonstrated dynamic-key caller so existing logging behavior remains exact.

likelyOwner.reason: The current once-only behavior and its focused tests appear to date to this person's merged environment-logging work.
